overview:
Fifteen panels agree that Lucid's foundations are right. The tone is calm, adult and guilt-free; the keycap design system is distinctive; placement and the AI-off states are honest; and teachers trust the Hebrew-speaker teaching content. The problems fall into five groups.
(1) Mixed Hebrew/English text. isolateLatin splits IPA and multi-sentence runs. Hebrew glosses repeat the English examples. English inside RTL cards takes three different alignments. At Pre-A1/A1 the English line outranks the Hebrew line that a beginner can actually read.
(2) The lesson player. The learn stage runs 7-14 phone screens. The resume button is hidden while the large buttons restart the lesson. End screens say 'כמעט שם' at 8% and skip past the daily plan. A wrong typed answer shows the key at once with no second try. Matching and the word bank punish single slips, and keyboard focus falls to <body>.
(3) Pace. All three games auto-advance and pay speed bonuses, against PRODUCT.md. On 10-minute days the lesson shrinks to 1-3 exercises and the learner's goals disappear.
(4) Large text and touch. There is no text-size choice before lesson 1. The progress bar shrinks to 2px at 150%. 'Enter' keycaps show on phones, the chrome covers inputs, and the scenario Continue button sits behind the tab bar.
(5) Honesty and fairness. Onboarding asks for AI consent and Settings says 'AI is on' on a site without AI. Review options can be answered by elimination. The writing checks miss errors that Lucid's own lessons teach. A passed level check claims a profile change that does not appear.
I checked the doubtful claims in the code and confirmed them: no pressed style for .key or .chip; no coarse-pointer rule for .kbd; setTimeout(next, 1100), 2500 ms and BACK_AFTER 1300 in the games; Math.min(0.5, ...) in answerPoints; lang=en dir=ltr on the transform source; fixed shuffle seeds in review.js; the Today minutes chip saving daily_minutes permanently; the lesson exit always going to Today; tables RTL whenever any header is Hebrew; and isolateLatin's output on the reported strings.
The work is split into 8 lanes by file ownership: shared controls and shell, lesson flow, exercise renderers, bilingual text and lesson content, first run and Today, review/hubs/settings, games, and real-life plus writing. Two cross-lane contracts are feature-detected, so each lane can merge on its own: ctl.reveal()/ctl.reopen() (from exercises to lesson-flow) and the relaxed_pace/game_speed_challenge settings keys (from practice-hubs to games). Shared CSS selectors are assigned in the lane titles. No lane edits tests/e2e/run.mjs or a11y.mjs; each lane adds its own tests/e2e/<lane>.mjs.
keep: Calm, adult, guilt-free voice ('יום חופש לא מוחק כלום', 'אין רצף שנשבר', 'אין ציון ואין ״נכשל״'), no mascot, no streaks, no confetti. Named by nearly every panel. No fix may add urgency, streak framing or celebratory animation.

Keycap design system: one orange Enter-key primary action, a 3px skirt press, the graphite deck, OKLCH tokens with at least 5:1 text contrast in light and dark. New states must reuse these tokens (design-visual, design-interaction, ux-accessibility).
The sticky verdict footer: the right answer first, 'למה?' folded, zero layout shift for a whole lesson (design-interaction, ux-writing-mobile, student-58).

A way out of every task without failing: 'לא יודע/ת', 'לא יכול/ה לדבר כרגע', and speaking that is never scored and is self-rated (ux-accessibility, student-16, student-44, student-58, student-68, teacher-special-ed).

Daily lesson parts that end on 'החלק של היום הושלם' with 'לעצור כאן' as the primary key and the place saved, plus Today's resume card with ?resume=1 (ux-research, student-19, student-44, ux-writing-mobile, teacher-special-ed).
Honest placement: 'לא יודע/ת' is encouraged, results are per skill, 'לא נבדק במבחן הזה' is shown, and the test can be resumed (ux-research, student-16, student-19, student-27, student-44).
Honest AI-off states in the tutor and the scenario AI tab, each pointing to what still works (design-visual, design-interaction, ux-accessibility, student-19, student-27).

Hebrew-speaker pitfall content and targeted wrong_feedback, which the teachers called accurate and contrastive. Reading answers quote the evidence line from the text (teacher-bagrut, teacher-adult-efl, student-16, student-44).

Reduced motion respected everywhere; no horizontal scroll at 320-1440px or at 130-150% text; skip link, focused stage h1, role=status verdicts, and a model focus-handling delete dialog (ux-accessibility, design-visual, student-68).

Games use one line-icon set with no cartoons. They offer 'play the words I missed' and 'add to review', and the picture game waits for keyboard players (design-visual, student-16, student-58, teacher-special-ed).
Dictation diff marks only the wrong letter; slow 'לאט' replay; transcript shown after answering (student-58, student-68, teacher-special-ed).
Bilingual desktop rail labels, the readable level rail with hatched placed-out levels, and Settings segmented controls with one-line help text (design-visual).
Writing lab: version comparison, parallel-prompt models, rebuttal moves, source packs with deliberate flaws, and the honest 'בדיקות אוטומטיות … יכולות לפספס' (teacher-academic).

lanes.title: Shell, navigation and shared controls. Owns the global component rules in css/app.css (.key, .chip, .option, .choice, .match-item, .pic-*, .mem-card base, .kbd, .seg, .deck, .tabbar, .top, .player-foot, .verdict, .empty, summary, focus rings, theme tokens). Other lanes do not edit these selectors.

items.title: Selected (latched) state on every pressable control
items.problem: Tapping True/False, a categorize chip or a speaking self-rating changes nothing on screen. aria-pressed=true is set, but app.css styles the pressed state only for .choice/.option/.match-item/.pic-* (lines 247, 370, 388, 916), not for .key or .chip. Hover, :active and tap-highlight rules are also missing on several skirted controls, and a wrong option keeps its blue keycap.
items.fix: css/app.css: add .key[aria-pressed='true'], .chip[aria-pressed='true'] { border-color: var(--cobalt); background: var(--cobalt-tint); } with the skirt held down to 1px (check the dark tokens too). Add one shared 'pressable' rule list for .key, .chip, .option, .choice, .match-item, .pic-tile, .pic-word, .mem-card and .seg button: a hover tint inside @media (hover:hover), a :active:not(:disabled) press, -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent, and one :focus-visible ring. In .option.is-right .k and .option.is-wrong .k, reset the keycap to the verdict colour.
items.acceptance: On #/lesson/a1-01 categorize, the tapped chip's computed background differs from the other chips. A tapped reading 'True' key looks latched, and so does the speaking 'אמרתי את זה בבירור' key. At 1440, hovering an .option changes its background. In 390 touch emulation, tapping a match tile shows no square blue halo. A wrong option shows no blue keycap.

items.problem: .key.ghost (css 182) has no border, fill or skirt. On touch, 'לא יודע/ת', 'רמז', 'לא יכול/ה לדבר כרגע', 'לא זוכר/ת' and 'להיום' read as captions, so the most important escape hatches are the hardest to find.

items.title: Play buttons show when they are playing and say when nothing played
items.problem: Pressing 'השמעה' leaves the button unchanged. With no English voice nothing plays and nothing says so, so silent mode and a missing voice look the same. At 150% the microphone notice opens scrolled past its heading. Help has nothing about sound.
items.fix: speech.js: say() dispatches a document event 'lucid:speech' with state start, end, error or silent (silent when no start fires within 1500 ms), and the module exports hasEnglishVoice(). app.js: one document listener sets aria-busy='true' and .is-playing on the [data-say], [data-say-text] or [data-say-tile] button that was clicked, until end. On silent, toast 'לא שומעים? בדקו את עוצמת הקול ומצב שקט. אם בדפדפן אין קול באנגלית, התמליל מוצג אחרי הבדיקה.'. The mic notice dialog opens scrolled to the top with focus on its heading. help.js: add the items 'לא שומעים את ההקראה' and 'איך מתרגלים דיבור בלי מיקרופון', and give 'נוחות קריאה' a link to #/settings.
items.acceptance: In headless Chrome with 0 voices, pressing 'השמעה' on a #/lesson/pa1-01 listening item shows the toast within 2s. With a voice, the button keeps the playing style while speaking and returns to normal afterwards. At 150%, the mic dialog opens with its heading visible. #/help lists the two new items.

items.title: A calm, compact feedback footer
items.problem: After a wrong answer the footer is a full-width pink panel with a red heading. At 150% it takes up to 49% of an 844px screen. 'בדיקה' sits bottom-left, then jumps when 'המשך' becomes full width. Options show right and wrong by colour only.

Constrain .inner to the player width. Set .verdict { max-height: 35dvh; overflow: auto }. At 30rem and below, put the primary key full width on its own row with the secondary keys in one compact row above it. Add a check or cross glyph via ::after on .option.is-right and .is-wrong, matching .game-mark.

items.title: Coming back resumes, never restarts
items.problem: When a lesson has a saved place, the intro's primary key is still 'בואו נלמד', and 'ישר לתרגול' calls go('practice') with a fresh queue, so it restarts at exercise 1 (lesson.js 247-251, 467). The resume banner sits at y≈975-1011, under the sticky footer. A restart discards the first-try record, so the end screen can say 100% after earlier mistakes. The plan note at the top is a 37-word paragraph (line 221).
items.fix: In showIntro, when resuming: put the banner first in the body and make the footer primary <button class='key enter' data-resume>להמשיך מתרגיל N מתוך M</button>. Secondary keys are 'להסבר' (data-go='learn') and 'להתחיל מההתחלה', which asks for confirmation through the components dialog. Hide 'ישר לתרגול' while resuming. In onKey, check [data-resume] first. On an explicit restart, copy the earlier first-try entries (r.first) into firstTry so the first try stays the first try. Shorten the plan note to one line under the key: 'היום: עד תרגיל 7 · כ-10 דק׳'.
items.acceptance: Start #/lesson/a2-01, answer 2 exercises, then reopen the lesson from #/path/A2 at 390x844 and at 768x1024 with 130% text. After a restart with all answers right, the end screen still counts the earlier wrong first tries.

When the lesson is passed and todayPlan() (a read-only import from adaptive.js) still has an unfinished block, the primary is 'להמשיך בתוכנית: <block> · N דק׳' (#/today) and 'לשיעור הבא' becomes secondary. items.title: Focus and Enter work for keyboard and screen-reader learners

items.title: Review options that can't be answered by elimination
items.problem: Meaning cards build their options with fixed seeds (review.js 81: shuffle(pool…, i + 1) and shuffle(…, i + 7)). The right answer therefore alternates between the same positions, and the same distractors repeat ('בין | סניף דואר | צעיר/ה' for 'cook', 'work' and 'drink'). They come from a tiny pool, mix parts of speech, and include long glosses ('כבשה (ברבים: …)').
items.fix: Seed the shuffle by card id plus the session date, so the right answer's position is uniformly random. Draw 3 distractors from the learner's learned words with the same pos (vocabulary entries carry pos), then from same-level curriculum vocabulary. Use the short gloss: the text before '(' or ';'.
items.acceptance: In two #/review sessions of 8 A1 cards, the right answer's position varies, no distractor set repeats between cards, a verb card shows only verb options (starting with ל-), and no option is longer than 4 words.

items.title: Automatic writing checks catch Hebrew-speaker errors and stay honest
items.problem: With AI off, the analyzer is the only writing feedback. On a B1 text it caught 4 of about 14 errors, and it misses errors that Lucid's own lessons teach: third-person -s, 'people was', 'alot'/'dont', their/there, 'for find', 'Although…, but', 'until' with a deadline, 'I will be happy if', 'has found in 2021', 'Rarely we see', 'Why we should…?', 'very important thing', 'this tools', and lowercase names. It flags the correct 'But by the time…, I had' as a run-on. It says 'לא נמצאו בעיות מוכרות' directly under a length warning.
items.fix:
writing-analyzer.js: add level-gated rules, each with a one-line Hebrew explanation, for:
- a singular subject, or every/each, followed by a base verb
- 'people was'
- alot, dont, doesnt, didnt and cant
- their/there before a noun
- for + base verb
- Although/Though … but
- until + a day, date or time (use 'by')
- 'I will be happy if' (use 'I'd be grateful if')
- 'I am writing you'
- a past time adverb with the present perfect
- a negative opener without inversion
- a statement-order wh-question
- a missing a/an before adjective + singular count noun
- this/these number agreement
- a lowercase name after 'my name is' or 'I live in'
From stage 8, add a highlighter for sweeping claims (all, every, never, everyone, nobody, proves). In the run-on test, skip one leading coordinator before the subordinator check, and add 'by the time' to the subordinators. The headline reads 'מצאנו N מהדברים שאנחנו בודקים' and never 'לא נמצאו בעיות' while a length or structure check fails.
items.acceptance: writing-analyzer.test.mjs has one case per rule, built from the panels' sentences. The we-06 sample text flags at least 10 of the 14 listed errors. 'But by the time the meeting started, I had written down every step' is not flagged. The status for a 3-word essay names the missing words instead of 'no problems'.

conflicts: Speed bonuses: student-16 enjoyed the speed bonus and 'שיא חדש!', but ux-accessibility, teacher-special-ed, student-68, student-44, teacher-adult-efl, teacher-bagrut and student-19 objected to it. PRODUCT.md promises 'no time pressure except opt-in timed writing'. Decision: speed bonuses and auto-advance are off by default. An opt-in 'אתגר מהירות' switch brings the bonus back, and personal bests are kept per mode (GM-1, PH-4).

When an answer commits: design-interaction offered either 'tap = answer everywhere' or 'select then check everywhere'. student-58, student-68 and teacher-special-ed want select-then-check. Decision: lessons, review and scenario practice all select, then check (PH-2, RW-1). Games keep tap-to-answer as a fast-feedback format, but say 'הבחירה נבדקת מיד' and drop the lesson keycap look on touch (GM-6).

Hebrew first at Pre-A1/A1 against PRODUCT.md's 'English as the destination': ux-research, student-44, teacher-adult-efl and teacher-special-ed want Hebrew to lead. Decision: only the meta-text (instructions and explanations) switches to Hebrew-primary at full support. English target content (examples, options, passages, tables) stays primary and visible, and the fade by level from A2 upward is unchanged (BL-3).

10-minute days: student-19 and student-16 want their goal content inside the 10 minutes, while student-44, student-58, student-68 and student-27 want a bigger lesson part. Decision: a lesson part is never fewer than 4 exercises and the review is capped at 3 minutes (TF-3). The goal item is offered as an optional one-tap line outside the budget (TF-4).

Games for placed learners: student-16 and student-19 want every level open, but the product principle is demonstrated ability. Decision: unlock up to the course level, since placement is evidence; levels above it stay gated by 70% accuracy (GM-3).
A quick game in the daily plan (student-16) against the research-based session template: the game is offered under 'רוצים עוד?' after the plan, not inside it (TF-2).

English alignment inside Hebrew cards: design-visual wants short English titles to share the Hebrew right edge, while student-27, teacher-academic and student-44 want English content left-aligned. Both are adopted under one rule: short English lines share the Hebrew edge, and dedicated LTR content blocks (examples, passages, tables, sources, checklists) are left-aligned (BL-4).

Review empty state: design-visual wants the full shell, but router.js makes #/review a bare player route on purpose. The route stays bare, and the empty state gets a heading, an action and an exit (PH-2).

Evidence rules: student-27 wants the grammar level to appear sooner, but the 2-day evidence rule is kept because demonstrated ability over activity is a product principle. Only the wording changes (TF-8).

Spelling accommodation: teacher-special-ed asks that spelling not be graded, but spelling is the learning target in dictation. Decision: wider tolerance (2 edits in words of 6+ letters, US/UK pairs, explained 'almost'), with spelling still graded (EX-7).

Second attempts: teacher-special-ed wants a second try on MCQs as well as typed answers, but MCQ retries reward guessing. Decision: the second try is for typed answers only (LF-6, EX-4). A gap with a word bank counts as a choice, not a typed answer: picking again among the chips left would be elimination, so it shows the answer at once (integration round 2).

Resume from the path (LF-1 against TF-11), decided in integration round 2: LF-1's acceptance reopens the lesson from #/path/A2 and expects the intro's resume key, while TF-11 adds ?resume=1 to path rows for lessons with a saved place, which goes straight to the saved exercise. Decision: the path row resumes directly (TF-11, never a restart, fewer taps). The intro's resume key (LF-1) serves every plain lesson link with no ?resume=1, such as Progress's 'השיעור הבא', the grammar pages and a bookmark. lesson-flow.mjs checks both: the path row lands on 3 מתוך 16, and the Progress link opens the intro with the resume key as the footer primary.

Numbered glosses (BL-1 against RW-10), recorded in integration round 2: BL-1's acceptance places the 'Chill' list number outside the English isolate on #/expressions, but RW-10 now renders numbered senses as an <ol>, so no app screen shows a Hebrew list number after English text. The isolateLatin rule ('chill. 3) Chill!') stays and is covered by tests/unit/i18n.test.mjs and by bilingual-text.mjs BL-1d, which renders the panel string through the app's own isolateLatin in the page. BL-1c now checks RW-10's list (no digits inside the English).
